scope: Matched Windows 1.26.51.1 / protocol 2193 camera control movement and selected look consumers. This is a bounded static contract, not all camera/input behavior or bit-for-bit physics parity.

identity.scope: C++ metadata and symbol addresses; memory layout is not wire serialization order; virtual overrides need base-slot verification.

facts.clear: Restores the current camera mode default; unsupported preset schemes use inherited/default selection.

entry_guard.fact: Compute float length of mMove. Return when length <= FLT_EPSILON (1.1920928955078125e-7).

scheme0_and_4.fact: No movement or rotation modification in this callback; their look handling is elsewhere.

facts: Compute heading from normalized horizontal mCameraOrientation and mMove using atan2f.
Reset actor pitch to0 and set actor yaw/head current/head previous to the wrapped combined heading.
Write mMove to zero sideways and original move magnitude forward; input flags/raw state are not rewritten.
Reset actor pitch to0; retain actor yaw.
Compute camera horizontal heading minus actor yaw.

Rotate mMove into actor-local coordinates using the existing 65536-entry sine table: sideways = cos(delta)*oldSideways - sin(delta)*oldForward; forward = sin(delta)*oldSideways + cos(delta)*oldForward.
Sine index computes degrees*0.01745329238474369 then *10430.3779296875 and truncates to integer; cosine adds16384 before truncation. Native sideways uses left-positive; Perlin stores right-positive.
If nonzero move length <=0.1, write both movement components to0 and retain pitch/yaw.
Otherwise reset pitch to0. Let q=1-forward; t=q if forward>=0, else t=2-q. The subtraction order is preserved.
If t>0.23, compute ease-out-cubic t as 1+(t-1)^3; multiply by10 degrees. Native sideways<0 adds the amount to yaw; sideways>=0 subtracts it.
If t>0.66, write both movement components to0; otherwise keep both original components.
Copy actor yaw into current and previous head yaw. Raw input flags are not modified.
Client input update calls calculateMoveVector at0x6698912 and stores mMove at0x6698920/0x669892e.
calculateMoveVector0x4495e0 normalizes overlength analog input and applies existing sneak scaling.

Camera transform registration precedes item-use attenuation. The ordinary category collection preserves insertion order; see slow_falling_findings.json for the collection adapter and iteration anchors.
ordering.qualification: The strict input adapter and common camera/item adapter share the ordinary system collection; special replay/filter schedules and all touch/UI processing have not been exhaustively traced.

facts: Always dispatches a camera look event before the control-scheme-specific tail.
The tail handles schemes0,2,4;1/3 do not take its actor-yaw update branches.
For2/4, nonzero input direction is combined with horizontal camera orientation and writes actor yaw plus current/previous head yaw.
Mouse mode1 with option0x187=false instead reads MoveInput.mLookDelta. Option name and the source of its screen-projection direction remain unresolved.
The direction magnitude-squared gate is FLT_EPSILON; normalization uses minimum length0.0001.
unresolved: Exact mouse pointer unprojection and screen-space input preparation.
Absolute gamepad/right-stick mapping and full-keyboard alternate path.
OptionID metadata contains no enumerator names for IDs4,5,391.
All redirect-camera component combinations for scheme0.

packet327_pitch_reset.fact: Each valid scheme2/4 packet resets local actor pitch, including repeated values. Other handler facts are retained in packet_contracts.json.

implemented: Scheme0 no longer replaces actor yaw with detached camera yaw.
Movement callback1/2/3 follows normalized/sneak-scaled input; item attenuation follows it.
Scheme2 rotates effective movement while retaining actor yaw.
Scheme3 applies recovered deadzone, cubic turn amount and travel cutoff.
The existing Update loop applies forced pitch as well as forced yaw to actor view.
Entering2/4 and explicit repeat requests can reset idle pitch. Root camera bridge supplies each packet reset request.
Direction flags and raw/analog vectors retain the original effective physical input rather than remapped movement.
MoveInput carries optional independent cameraOrientation. The sender copies it verbatim and retains the existing actor-derived fallback when absent.
SetCameraView accepts the active camera direction and clearing it restores the fallback. Nonfinite direction components reject the send before consuming tick/queued actions.
limits: Perlin receives camera heading as yaw; the native horizontal orientation-vector normalization/atan2 path can differ at vertical or degenerate camera directions.
The existing sine table is reused; all transcendental and camera orientation construction paths have not been proved bit-identical.
Input mode2/4 absolute screen/stick aim is a separate incomplete path; this patch does not claim to implement it.
Riding/sleep-specific transforms remain outside this local walking callback integration.
2193 is the native reference; common behavior is tested through944/2193/2225 packet encodings, which does not independently prove identical native semantics in each version.
Render-time camera direction sampling is provided by the parent camera integration; exact native interpolation timing remains unproven.

validation.integration: 120 added movement_protocol checks across944,2193,2225; full app build/test delegated to parent. Update runtime result after integration.
checks: Locked player-relative idle/forward/strafe/clear behavior with detached yaw.
Independent actor yaw and rotated diagonal movement for scheme2.
Scheme3 turn signs, forward/back, native cubic shallow turn, item-use ordering, sneak ordering, deadzone boundary.
Idle2/4 entry and explicit repeated pitch reset.
Independent camera direction with unchanged actor/interaction rotation, clearing fallback and invalid-direction send rejection preserving pending movement state.
validation.unit: Standalone g++ -std=c++20 -Isrc tests/move_input_selftest.cpp executable passed, including10 new independent-direction validation checks.

copies.fact: Copies the already transformed effective movement vector.

copies.qualification: Its producer and exact aiming semantics are not yet traced; no Perlin interactRotation change is inferred.

copies.fact: Copies all three camera direction components verbatim, independently of actor rotation.

unresolved: Exact stage and interpolation time at which the current input camera samples its orientation; a copy contract is not proof of render sampling timing.
